title: Jimmy Knepper, the Town Hall copyist dispute and the open recording session
summary: Mingus gives his version of the Knepper incident and explains the planned open recording session.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, Jimmy Hepper held me up -- from getting -- he's always worked in a certain capacity as a copyist, where I would use my extended forms.
Yeah.
He used to do it for Town Hall.
Why?

I don't know. And he was -- I didn't really hit Jimmy, but Jimmy was leaving the door, and I opened the door in his face, and it bumped his teeth out. I didn't hit him. He claims I hit him. That whole thing was a farce. They knew I was doing recording and writing music, and they called me to do an Ellington date which slowed me down. I would have been ready but for that Ellington date.
Yeah. Wasn't that the concert when you said onstage that if any people wanted their money back, they could get it?
Yeah, because it was not supposed to have been a concert.
Yeah.
It's supposed to have been an open recording session, free for people to come in who wanted to see how a recording session went down.
That's right.

I got the idea from watching Ellington record the same way in California, with his first record that he did for Columbia in California. He had the copiers on the stage. He used a theatre, and people who knew about it got to come through the door in the back, the few people that heard about it got to come to the recording session.
Yeah.
So I wanted to do the same thing. I
think I must have struck the concert people, like George (unintelligible), because he came -- because I was getting the record company to pay for everything.
Yeah. United Artists, isn't it?
Yeah, they wanted to stop that.
Why?
I can't tell you why,man, why they stopped --
Yeah.
Ballroom dancing. They stopped ballroom dancing because it caused integration.
Yeah.
And they made it a concert called Jazz Concert. They really stopped (inaudible), because everybody was going for it. Maybe the record strike did it, I don't know.
